explanations.explanation: That's what the LORD says: "you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land…" (Numbers 33:52). Not some of them. All of them. When the LORD gives Moses an instruction, He doesn't leave a loose end hanging around like a stray crumb.

I get the thought, friend. Signing a paper sounds peaceful and tidy. But the LORD's words to Israel are "you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land…" (Numbers 33:52), and a treaty isn't anywhere in that sentence.

That's a kind idea, and I like where your heart is. Here, though, the text gives a different instruction: "you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land…" (Numbers 33:52). Teaching them isn't part of what the LORD tells Moses to say here.
Yes, destroy. The LORD tells Israel to "destroy all their carved images and cast idols…" (Numbers 33:52). Those idols aren't going home as souvenirs. The command is clear and it's the whole job.

Oh, I see the temptation. Some folks keep everything, and I once kept a rubber band for years just in case. But the LORD says to "destroy all their carved images and cast idols…" (Numbers 33:52). Nothing about keeping them.

Nice business brain, friend! But no yard sale here. The LORD says Israel must "destroy all their carved images and cast idols…" (Numbers 33:52). Destroying them is the instruction, and selling isn't on the list.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says the opposite. He tells Israel to "demolish all their high places" (Numbers 33:52). Demolish means they don't stay standing.

That's right, it's false. The LORD says Israel must "demolish all their high places" (Numbers 33:52). High places are the spots the Canaanites used for their idols, and the instruction is to take them down. No leaving a few up for decoration.

explanations.answer: He has given them the land
explanations.explanation: Right on the money. The LORD says, "for I have given you the land to possess" (Numbers 33:53). The reason is that He gave it, plain and simple. Israel doesn't earn it by being impressive.

Good guess, since armies feel like the usual answer. But the LORD never mentions Israel's army here. His reason is "for I have given you the land to possess" (Numbers 33:53). The land is a gift, not a prize for muscle.
I feel that one, friend. After my years in a drawer, I know what waiting feels like. But the LORD doesn't give that as the reason. He says, "for I have given you the land to possess" (Numbers 33:53).

That's it. The LORD says, "you are to divide the land by lot according to your clans" (Numbers 33:54). And "Whatever falls to each one by lot will be his." No arguing over who got the better corner, because the lot settled it.
Reasonable guess, friend. Wise elders sounds like a fine plan. But the LORD says to "divide the land by lot according to your clans" (Numbers 33:54). The lot decides, not anybody's pick.
A vote sounds fair, and it would also sound like a LOT of campaigning. But that's not what the LORD says. He tells Israel to "divide the land by lot according to your clans" (Numbers 33:54).

True! The LORD says, "Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one" (Numbers 33:54). The size of the clan matters for the size of the share. Lots decide where, and size decides how much.
Close, but it's true. The LORD says, "Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one" (Numbers 33:54). Bigger clan, bigger share. Smaller clan, smaller share.

Yes, harass. The LORD says those left in the land "will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle" (Numbers 33:55). Barbs and thorns aren't comfy things to carry around. That's a warning with some sting to it.

Nice thought, friend, but that isn't the word. The LORD says those left in the land "will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle" (Numbers 33:55). Barbs and thorns don't sound like helpers to me.

I wish it went that way, I really do. A warm welcome is my favorite thing. But the LORD says they "will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle" (Numbers 33:55).

explanations.answer: Do to Israel what He planned for Canaan
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The LORD says, "And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them" (Numbers 33:56). It's a serious line, so I'll let it be serious. The warning is real, and it comes with that big IF.

explanations.answer: Send Israel back into the wilderness
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd think that, since the wilderness is where Israel has been. But the LORD doesn't say that here. He says, "And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them" (Numbers 33:56).

explanations.answer: Give Israel a smaller share of land
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, since land is the topic. But the LORD's words go another way. He says, "And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them" (Numbers 33:56). Nothing there about a smaller share.

explanations.answer: The other tribes already have their land
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says, "For the tribes of the Reubenites and Gadites, along with the half-tribe of Manasseh, have already received their inheritance" (Numbers 34:14). That leaves nine and a half tribes still waiting on their shares. The math works out, even with a half in it.

explanations.answer: The other tribes chose to stay in Egypt
explanations.explanation: Oh no, friend, not Egypt! Moses gives a different reason. He says, "For the tribes of the Reubenites and Gadites, along with the half-tribe of Manasseh, have already received their inheritance" (Numbers 34:14). They aren't back in Egypt. They already have land.

explanations.answer: The other tribes were too small to count
explanations.explanation: That one feels a little unfair to those tribes, doesn't it? Moses never says they're too small. He says they "have already received their inheritance" (Numbers 34:14). Their land is settled, so they aren't left out.

True. Moses says, "These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, toward the sunrise" (Numbers 34:15). Those tribes are Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Their land sits on the east side of the river.

It's actually true, friend. Moses says, "These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, toward the sunrise" (Numbers 34:15). That's Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. Their land is already theirs.
Yes! The LORD says, "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun" (Numbers 34:17). Eleazar is the priest, and Joshua is the son of Nun. These two are the ones named to assign the land.

Good names, friend, but not the ones the LORD picks here. He says the men to assign the land are "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun" (Numbers 34:17). Eleazar, the priest, and Joshua, the son of Nun, are the pair.
Nice try pulling names from the Bible's deep bench! But the LORD names someone else. He says, "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun" (Numbers 34:17). Those are the two for this job.

That's right. The LORD says, "Appoint one leader from each tribe to distribute the land" (Numbers 34:18). Every tribe gets someone of its own at the table. Nobody has to hope the other tribes remembered them.
Good guess, friend, since land and cities go together. But the LORD says, "Appoint one leader from each tribe to distribute the land" (Numbers 34:18). The leaders come from the tribes.

That would be a LOT of leaders, friend. A whole kitchen full! But the LORD says, "Appoint one leader from each tribe to distribute the land" (Numbers 34:18). It's one per tribe, not one per household.
